Let me analyze this specification. It's about Spring Cloud Data Flow (s-c-d / SCDF) and Spring Cloud Stream (s-c-s) related work. The user stories are:

- U1: Move Kafka @Rule (JUnit test rule) to a separate repo, so test fixtures can be consumed in different projects.
- U2: Move Rabbit @Rule to a separate repo.
- U3: Admin REST APIs consistent across platforms (Lattice, YARN, CF - Cloud Foundry).
- U4: Register artifacts as libraries, reference them in include/exclude statements.
- U5: Named channels option - create streaming pipelines without source or sink modules (i.e., tap into existing middleware destinations).
- U6: Add test coverage for StreamController, verify API contracts at build time.
- U7: Prevent creating streams with duplicate names - unique names enforced.
- U8: Kinesis module as a source module for streaming pipeline.

U4: Register artifacts as libraries, include/exclude statements. Add registration support (library artifact type), resolution in stream parsing for includes/excludes, REST endpoints, shell commands maybe. ~40-60 hours.

U5: Named channels: allow streams to bind to externally defined destinations without source/sink modules. Parser changes, deployment logic, docs, tests. ~40 hours.

U6: Test coverage for StreamController: write MockMvc tests verifying API contracts. ~24-32 hours.

U7: Prevent duplicate stream names: validation in controller/service, repository check, error handling, tests. ~8-12 hours.

U8: Kinesis source module: implement Spring Cloud Stream Kinesis binder? Actually "kinesis module ... source module" - implement a Kinesis source app/module (spring-cloud-stream-modules). Includes binder support possibly. Assume binder exists? Let's assume we implement the source module with binder; if binder doesn't exist that's huge. Reasonable assumption: implement Kinesis source module using AWS SDK/KCL, with tests, docs. ~40-60 hours.

Then:
11. Integration & system testing (24h)
12. Documentation (16h)
13. Release/deployment prep (8h)

technical_and_design_decisions: All work targets the Spring Cloud Data Flow (admin server, StreamController, module/artifact registry) and Spring Cloud Stream codebases; Java 8+ with Maven multi-module builds and JUnit 4.

U1/U2: Extract the Kafka and Rabbit JUnit @Rule test fixtures into two dedicated Git repositories (e.g., spring-cloud-stream-test-support-kafka and -rabbit), each with a standalone Maven build publishing versioned artifacts; existing projects switch from embedded copies to consuming the published artifacts.

U3: Introduce a platform-neutral App Deployer SPI between the admin REST layer and runtime platforms; the admin REST API delegates to this SPI so behavior is identical across Cloud Foundry, YARN, and Lattice, each backed by a platform-specific deployer implementation.

U4: Extend the artifact registry with a 'library' artifact type identified by Maven coordinates; include/exclude statements in stream definitions are resolved at definition/deployment time against registered libraries.

U5: Support named channels via a DSL/parser extension that binds stream definitions directly to externally managed middleware destinations (topics/queues) without requiring source or sink modules; deployer binds named channels using standard binder destination properties.
U6: StreamController API contracts verified with Spring MockMvc-based tests executed in the build (no live middleware required).
U7: Stream name uniqueness enforced in the controller/service layer backed by the stream definition repository; violations return HTTP 409 Conflict with a clear error message.

U8: Kinesis source implemented as a Spring Cloud Stream source module using the AWS Kinesis Client Library (KCL) with externalized configuration properties (stream name, region, credentials, checkpointing).
assumptions: A single developer performs all work; estimates are pure effort (work-hours) excluding review queues, meetings, and wait time.
Existing Spring Cloud Data Flow / Spring Cloud Stream codebases (admin server, StreamController, DSL parser, module registry) are available and buildable as the starting point.

Test infrastructure is available: embedded Kafka/Rabbit or Docker-based brokers for U1/U2, LocalStack (or equivalent AWS mock) for Kinesis in U8, and accessible CF, YARN, and Lattice test environments for U3.
New repositories for U1/U2 are created under the existing GitHub organization and reuse the established CI (Travis/Jenkins) and artifact publishing (snapshot/milestone) setup.
Scope covers server-side code, DSL/parser, REST API, shell commands, and reference documentation; no web dashboard (UI) work is required.
Backward compatibility must be preserved for existing stream definitions and REST clients.
No formal performance/load testing or security audit is in scope beyond standard unit/integration tests.

activities.activity_description: Analyze the eight user stories, map them to affected components (test fixtures, admin server, deployer SPI, registry, DSL parser, StreamController, Kinesis module), define acceptance criteria, and sequence the work.

Design the App Deployer SPI abstraction (U3), the library registration and include/exclude resolution model (U4), the named-channel DSL extension (U5), and the extracted test-fixture artifact structure (U1/U2); produce design notes and interface sketches.

activities.activity_name: U1: Extract Kafka @Rule to separate repository
activities.activity_description: Create the new repository, move the Kafka JUnit rule and supporting classes, set up a standalone Maven build and artifact publishing, update spring-cloud-stream consumers to depend on the published artifact, adapt tests, and write README/docs.

activities.activity_name: U2: Extract Rabbit @Rule to separate repository
activities.activity_description: Repeat the extraction pattern for the Rabbit JUnit rule: new repository, standalone build and publishing, consumer migration to the external artifact, test adaptation, and documentation (benefits from U1 experience).

activities.activity_name: U3: Consistent admin REST APIs across Lattice, YARN, and Cloud Foundry
activities.activity_description: Define the platform-neutral App Deployer SPI, refactor the admin REST layer to delegate to it, implement/align the Cloud Foundry, YARN, and Lattice deployer implementations, normalize status/error mapping, and add per-platform integration tests proving consistent REST behavior.

activities.activity_name: U4: Library artifact registration with include/exclude support
activities.activity_description: Add a 'library' artifact type to the registry with Maven coordinate resolution, implement include/exclude resolution during stream definition parsing and deployment, add REST endpoints and shell commands for library registration, plus unit/integration tests and docs.

activities.activity_name: U5: Named channels for pipelines without source/sink modules
activities.activity_description: Extend the stream DSL/parser to reference externally managed destinations as named channels, implement binder binding/validation logic for named channels at deployment time, handle error cases (missing destination, conflicts), and add tests and reference documentation.

activities.activity_name: U6: StreamController API contract test coverage
activities.activity_description: Write comprehensive MockMvc-based tests for all StreamController endpoints (create, list, get, deploy, undeploy, destroy, validation errors), asserting HTTP status codes, payloads, and error contracts so they run at build time.

Add duplicate-name validation in the controller/service layer backed by the stream definition repository, map violations to HTTP 409 with a clear message, and add unit and API tests covering create/rename edge cases.

Implement the Kinesis source module using the AWS Kinesis Client Library (KCL): message consumption and mapping to Spring Messaging, externalized configuration properties (stream, region, credentials, checkpointing), binder integration, unit/integration tests against a LocalStack-style mock, and documentation.

End-to-end verification of the increment: build and deploy sample streams exercising named channels, library include/exclude, and the Kinesis source; verify admin REST consistency across the three platforms; regression-run the full build.

Update reference documentation and READMEs for the new test-fixture repositories, deployer SPI and platform notes, library registration, named channels, duplicate-name behavior, StreamController contracts, and the Kinesis source; add sample stream definitions.

activities.activity_name: CI setup for new repositories and release preparation
activities.activity_description: Configure CI pipelines and artifact publishing for the two new test-fixture repositories, wire new modules into the main build, perform version alignment, changelog, and release-candidate builds.
